shots.say: Why do things fall down? Why not up?
Drop a ball, and down it goes. Every time!
Hi! I'm Gizmo. Let's find out why things fall down!
Gizmo Explains!
Welcome to my lab, science fans!
Today, we learn about a pull that you can not see!
Look at this apple tree in the meadow.
One apple lets go of its branch. Down it falls, onto the grass!
Which way does the apple fall? Up, or down?
Down! Things always fall down, toward the ground.
But why? What pulls them down? Let's think!
It is a force called gravity!
Gravity is an invisible pull. It pulls things toward each other.
Can we see gravity? Yes, or no?
Gravity is invisible! We drew arrows, so you can see the pull.
The Earth pulls everything toward its middle, its center.
So people all around the Earth stand on the ground!
Gravity pulled the apple down, toward the Earth's center.
Plop! There it is, down on the grass.
Which way does gravity pull? Toward the Earth's center, or up to the sky?
Hop up, just a little! Gravity brings you back down.
Point down to the ground, where gravity pulls!
Say it with me. Gravity pulls things down!
What keeps you on the ground? Gravity, or glue?
Gravity! It keeps you on the ground, and makes things fall.
Here is a heavy ball, and a light ball.
We drop them together. Which lands first? The heavy one, or do they land together?
Together! Dropped from the same height, they land at the same time.
Wow! Gravity speeds up heavy things and light things the same way.
Let's try it again. Ready? Drop!
But look at this feather. It floats down, slowly.
A ball and a feather. Which lands first?
Hmm, why is the feather so slow? Let's think!
The ball! The air slows the feather down.
The air pushes on the feather, so it drifts down, side to side.
What slows the feather down? The air, or the ground?
Float your hands down slowly, like a feather!
Now, think of a place with no air at all.
With no air, we drop a rock and a feather. Which lands first?
They land at exactly the same time! No air slows the feather.
Say it with me. The air slows the feather!
Heavy and light fall together. Only the air slows a feather down.
Here is a big surprise. Everything that is made of stuff has gravity!
A little ball has a little bit of gravity, just a tiny pull.
Does a little ball have gravity? Yes, or no?
Things with more stuff, more mass, have more gravity.
You have gravity too, and so do I!
Which has more gravity? A ball, or the big Earth?
The Earth! It is so big, its pull holds all of us down.
Make a big round Earth with your arms!
Now look up, into space. There is the Moon, way up high!
The Moon goes around, and around, the Earth.
Point up to the Moon in the sky!
Earth's gravity keeps the Moon going around the Earth.
What goes around the Earth? The Moon, or a cloud?
And the Sun's gravity keeps the Earth, and all the planets, going around the Sun!
Turn around slowly, like the Moon going around!
Say it with me. Everything has gravity!
So when a ball falls down in the park, now you know why!
It is gravity, pulling it toward the Earth!
Quiz time! Let's remember what we learned.
Which way does an apple fall from a tree? Up, or down?
Down! Gravity pulls it toward the ground.
Drop a heavy ball and a light ball. Which lands first? Heavy, or together?
Together! They land at the same time.
What keeps the Moon going around the Earth? Gravity, or a rope?
Gravity! Round and round goes the Moon.
Apples, balls, and the Moon. That is gravity! Thanks for exploring with me!
Gizmo Explains!
